docs.title: Dependency conflicts
docs.text:
Maven or Gradle reports conflicts with the AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud SDKs. Import io.tileverse:tileverse-bom: it imports the cloud SDK versions used to build and test the library. Declare it before any other cloud SDK BOM, because Maven takes a managed version from the first BOM declaring it.

<dependencyManagement>
    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.tileverse</groupId>
            <artifactId>tileverse-bom</artifactId>
            <version>2.1.0</version>
            <type>pom</type>
            <scope>import</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>

docs.title: Missing backend module
docs.text: Each cloud backend lives in its own module. Without it, a URI of its scheme fails to open with No suitable provider found for URI, and code that uses its SDK types fails with ClassNotFoundException. Add tileverse-storage-s3, tileverse-storage-azure, tileverse-storage-gcs, or tileverse-storage-all for all three. Getting Started lists the modules.

docs.title: S3 credentials
docs.text:
With no credential parameter, the S3 backend uses the AWS default credential chain, and reports Unable to load credentials ... when the chain finds none. Provide credentials in one of these ways:

  • Environment variables: 
    export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-access-key
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret-key
export AWS_REGION=us-west-2
  • The credentials file, ~/.aws/credentials: 
    [default]
aws_access_key_id = your-access-key
aws_secret_access_key = your-secret-key
  • An IAM role, on EC2, ECS or EKS. Nothing to configure.

The chain never falls back to anonymous access. To read a public bucket, set storage.s3.anonymous=true. Authenticate lists all the options.

docs.title: Access denied
docs.text:
AccessDeniedException means the identity lacks a permission on the object, such as s3:GetObject on S3. On S3, a missing object also returns 403 when the identity may not list the bucket.

On AWS, a request sent to the wrong region is sent again to the region of the bucket. Presigned URLs and S3-compatible services need the right region: set storage.s3.region.

docs.title: Azure authentication
docs.text:
AuthenticationFailed means the credentials do not match the account. Check the connection string or the account key, and the expiry of a SAS token. The se field of the token holds its expiry time:

echo "$SAS_TOKEN" | tr '&' '\n' | grep '^se='

docs.title: GCS credentials
docs.text:
With storage.gcs.anonymous unset, opening a GCS Storage fails with No Application Default Credentials found when no credentials are found. Set up Application Default Credentials:

export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/service-account.json
# or, for your own account:
gcloud auth application-default login

To read a public bucket, set storage.gcs.anonymous=true. An AccessDeniedException caused by a GCS error 403 means the identity lacks a permission on the bucket.

docs.title: Slow reads
docs.text: Each remote read pays a round trip. Cache the reads, with CachingRangeReader.of(reader) or with storage.caching.enabled=true on the configuration passed to StorageFactory.open. The file backend ignores that parameter. For parts of a file read again and again, such as a header or an index, declare block-aligned regions. Configure for performance describes both.

docs.title: Memory and the cache
docs.text:
The shared range cache holds at most 20% of the maximum heap, weighed by cached bytes, and an entry expires 60 seconds after its last access. The cache stays empty until readers are wrapped in a CachingRangeReader or storage.caching.enabled is set.

  • Each CacheManager.newInstance() owns a cache with a budget of its own. Readers built without an explicit manager share the default one: keep it that way.
  • A job reading a file front to back gains nothing from the cache, and fills it with bytes read once. Use the reader returned by Storage.openRangeReader directly.
  • BlockAlignedRangeReader.alignWholeFile() turns each read inside the file into cached blocks. Declare only the regions read repeatedly, and let tile or row payloads pass through as exact ranges.

docs.title: Low cache hit rate
docs.text:
The cache keys on the exact (offset, length) of a read. Two reads share an entry only when they ask for the same range, or when they fall in the same block of a block-aligned region. An entry unused for 60 seconds expires, and a hit rate measured across idle periods drops for that reason alone.

import io.tileverse.cache.CacheStats;
import io.tileverse.storage.cache.CachingRangeReader;

if (reader instanceof CachingRangeReader cachingReader) {
    CacheStats stats = cachingReader.getCacheStats();
    System.out.printf("hit rate %.2f%%, %d hits, %d misses, %d evictions, %d entries%n",
            stats.hitRate() * 100, stats.hitCount(), stats.missCount(), stats.evictionCount(), stats.entryCount());
}

The statistics cover the shared cache of the CacheManager, across the readers using it, not this reader alone.

docs.title: Connection timeouts
docs.text:
The HTTP backend reports TransientStorageException: Connection timeout after 5000 milliseconds. Raise storage.http.timeout-millis, 5000 by default:

Properties props = new Properties();
props.setProperty("storage.http.timeout-millis", "30000");

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(parent, props);
        RangeReader reader = storage.openRangeReader(leaf)) {
    // ...
}

For S3, raise the io.tileverse.storage.s3-http-client.connection-timeout system property, 2 seconds by default; see System Properties. For a client setting without a parameter, build the SDK client yourself and pass it to the provider, as described in Configure for performance.

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text:
The HTTP and S3 backends use the proxy settings of the JVM:

-Dhttps.proxyHost=proxy.company.com -Dhttps.proxyPort=8080

The S3 backend also reads the http_proxy, https_proxy and no_proxy environment variables, in lowercase only. For another backend, configure the proxy on its SDK client and pass the client to the provider, as described in Authenticate.

docs.title: TLS certificates
docs.text:
For an HTTPS endpoint with a self-signed certificate or a private CA, the HTTP, Azure and GCS backends use the trust store of the JVM. Add the certificate to it:

keytool -import -alias custom-cert -file cert.crt -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts

The S3 backend uses the trust store of the operating system instead. For a MinIO or Ceph service with a private CA, install the CA in the operating system. The Java SDK does not read AWS_CA_BUNDLE.

During development, storage.http.trust-all-certificates=true disables the certificate checks of the HTTP backend; the other backends have no such setting. Never use it in production.

docs.title: S3-compatible services without an ETag header
docs.text: A gateway exporting an existing tree of files may serve objects without an ETag header: the objects placed directly in its backend have none, and the objects written through the S3 API have one. A Storage opened from a URI or a StorageConfig reads both. A client built with S3AsyncClient.crtBuilder() and passed to S3StorageProvider.open(URI, S3AsyncClient) fails with Response missing required ETag header. Pass a client built with S3AsyncClient.builder() instead.

docs.title: S3 requests waiting for a connection
docs.text:
S3 requests fail with Connection Manager failed to acquire a connection within the defined timeout. The S3 storages opened from a URI or a StorageConfig send their requests through one connection pool per host, shared by the process. A request waits 30 seconds for a free connection, then fails. The SDK retries some of those failures, up to 3 times each; when many requests fail together, most of them get no retry.

Raise the pool size, io.tileverse.storage.s3-http-client.max-concurrency, or keep fewer requests in flight against the host: lower storage.batch.max-in-flight-fetches (default 8) or the number of concurrent readers. A multipart upload keeps an eighth of the pool in flight while it runs. System Properties gives the default pool size.

docs.title: Too many open files
docs.text:
A server opening many local readers fails with IOException: Too many open files. A local reader holds a file descriptor only while its channel is open: from the first read until storage.file.idle-timeout (default 60 seconds) elapses with no read in progress. Descriptors pile up when many readers are read within the same minute, or when readers are opened and never closed.

  • Close readers when a request is done with them. A closed reader never reopens its channel.
  • Shorten the idle timeout, for example storage.file.idle-timeout=PT10S.
  • Raise the descriptor limit (ulimit -n) when the working set is that large.

docs.title: Stale NFS file handles
docs.text:
Reads of a file on an NFS or SMB mount fail after the export was remounted or the file was replaced on the server. The operating system reports Stale file handle (Linux) or Stale NFS file handle (macOS, BSD).

Range reads recover by themselves: the reader drops the stale channel, opens the file again by its real path, and resumes after the bytes already read, up to three attempts per call. A read that still fails reports Read failed after 3 attempts: the mount stays stale.

An AccessDeniedException on a local file means the process cannot read it: check the permissions of the file.

docs.title: Debug logging
docs.text:
Set the log level of io.tileverse.storage to DEBUG in your logging configuration. The SDKs log under software.amazon.awssdk (S3), com.azure (Azure) and com.google.cloud (GCS).

-Djdk.httpclient.HttpClient.log=requests,headers logs the requests and headers of the JDK HTTP client, used by the HTTP and Azure backends.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: Search the GitHub issues. To report a problem, include the library version, the Java version, the full error message and stack trace, and a minimal example.

docs.title: Use each backend
docs.text: This page shows the smallest end-to-end snippet for each supported backend, and what is particular to each. All snippets use the same Storage API; only the URI changes.

docs.title: Local filesystem
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.storage.ReadHandle;
import io.tileverse.storage.Storage;
import io.tileverse.storage.StorageEntry;
import io.tileverse.storage.StorageFactory;
import java.net.URI;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.util.stream.Stream;

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("file:///data/cache/"))) {
    storage.put("hello.txt", "world".getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
    try (Stream<StorageEntry> entries = storage.list("**/*.txt")) {
        entries.forEach(entry -> System.out.println(entry.key()));
    }
    try (ReadHandle r = storage.read("hello.txt")) {
        byte[] read = r.content().readAllBytes();
    }
}

A local reader opens a file channel on its first read and closes it after storage.file.idle-timeout (default 60 seconds) with no read in progress. It holds a file descriptor only while the channel is open, and a closed reader never reopens one. Closing a FileStorage leaves the readers obtained from it usable.

Range reads of local files respond to thread interrupts. A read on an interrupted thread fails with a StorageException, and the interrupt flag stays set. An interrupt during a read closes the file channel shared by the readers of that file; the other readers continue on a new channel. Streaming reads and writes do not respond to interrupts.

docs.title: HTTP / HTTPS (read-only)
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.storage.ReadHandle;
import io.tileverse.storage.ReadOptions;
import io.tileverse.storage.RangeReader;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("https://example.com/data/"))) {
    // Range read via the existing RangeReader API
    try (RangeReader reader = storage.openRangeReader("file.bin")) {
        ByteBuffer buf = reader.readRange(0, 1024);
    }
    // Streaming read with offset
    try (ReadHandle r = storage.read("file.bin", ReadOptions.fromOffset(1024))) {
        byte[] tail = r.content().readAllBytes();
    }
    // Listing and writes throw UnsupportedCapabilityException
}

The HTTP backend does not follow redirects: a 3xx answer fails the read with Redirect not followed. Object stores and CDNs often answer a presigned or edge URL with a 302; open the final URL instead.

docs.title: AWS S3
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.storage.WriteOptions;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.time.Duration;
import java.util.Optional;

// General-purpose bucket
try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("s3://my-bucket/datasets/v3/"))) {
    storage.put("year=2024/file.parquet", Path.of("/local/file.parquet"), WriteOptions.defaults());
    try (Stream<StorageEntry> entries = storage.list("year=2024/**")) {
        entries.forEach(e -> System.out.println(e.key()));
    }
}

// S3 Express One Zone (Directory Bucket): same code, bucket name encodes the AZ
try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(
        URI.create("s3://my-bucket--usw2-az1--x-s3/datasets/"))) {
    // Capabilities reflect Express constraints: 5-min presign max, no versioning
    Optional<Duration> maxTtl = storage.capabilities().maxPresignTtl();
    System.out.println(maxTtl); // Optional[PT5M]
}

Authentication uses the AWS default credential chain unless you set storage.s3.anonymous=true, the storage.s3.aws-access-key-id / storage.s3.aws-secret-access-key pair, or storage.s3.default-credentials-profile. Public buckets need storage.s3.anonymous=true.

S3 Express One Zone differs from general-purpose buckets in three ways: its ETags are random strings rather than MD5 digests, its presigned URLs last at most 5 minutes, and its listings are not in lexicographic order.

docs.title: S3-compatible services
docs.text:
The S3 backend serves any service speaking the S3 API. Address the service in one of two forms:

  • Keep the URL of the service and name the provider: http(s)://endpoint/bucket/key with storage.provider=s3. The endpoint comes from the URL. With no provider named, the same URL opens the read-only HTTP backend.
  • Keep a canonical s3://bucket/key URI and point it at the service with storage.s3.endpoint, as below. Path-style addressing is enabled automatically.

Credentials and region come from the same parameters as for AWS:

import java.util.Properties;

Properties props = new Properties();
props.setProperty("storage.s3.endpoint", "http://localhost:9000"); // MinIO
props.setProperty("storage.s3.aws-access-key-id", "minioadmin");
props.setProperty("storage.s3.aws-secret-access-key", "minioadmin");
props.setProperty("storage.s3.region", "us-east-1");

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("s3://my-bucket/datasets/"), props)) {
    storage.put("file.parquet", Path.of("/local/file.parquet"), WriteOptions.defaults());
}

See Configure - Custom endpoint for how storage.s3.endpoint interacts with force-path-style, region, and credentials.

Tested or known to work:

Service Service URL Notes MinIO http://host:9000/bucket/key Self-hosted. Garage http://host:3900/bucket/key Self-hosted; the test suite runs against it. Ceph RADOS Gateway (RGW) https://rgw.example.com/bucket/key Common in OpenStack and on-premises deployments. OpenStack Swift (via s3api middleware) https://swift.example.com/bucket/key The native Swift API is not supported. Cloudflare R2 https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/bucket/key Set storage.s3.region=auto. Backblaze B2 https://s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com/bucket/key Wasabi https://s3.<region>.wasabisys.com/bucket/key DigitalOcean Spaces https://<region>.digitaloceanspaces.com/bucket/key IBM Cloud Object Storage https://s3.<region>.cloud-object-storage.appdomain.cloud/bucket/key Use the public S3 endpoint, not the legacy Swift one. Linode Object Storage https://<region>.linodeobjects.com/bucket/key OVHcloud Object Storage (S3 endpoint) https://s3.<region>.cloud.ovh.net/bucket/key OVH offers both S3 and Swift endpoints; use the S3 one.

Native protocols such as OpenStack Swift, Azure Files (SMB), HDFS or FTP are out of scope; Why tileverse-storage? explains why.

docs.title: Azure Blob Storage
docs.text:
import java.time.Duration;

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("az://myaccount/my-container/datasets/"))) {

    // Generate a SAS-based presigned URL valid for 15 minutes
    if (storage.capabilities().presignedUrls()) {
        URI presigned = storage.presignGet("file.bin", Duration.ofMinutes(15));
    }
}

Authentication uses DefaultAzureCredential by default (env vars, managed identity, Azure CLI). Provide storage.azure.connection-string, storage.azure.account-key or storage.azure.sas-token for explicit credentials, or storage.azure.anonymous=true for a public container.

az://account/container resolves to the public https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net endpoint. The https:// URL of a container opens this backend when storage.provider=azure is set; the endpoint then comes from the URL. Blobs of the root container are reached through its name, $root: az://account/$root/. Set storage.azure.endpoint to redirect an az:// URI to an emulator, a sovereign cloud (Azure Government, Azure China), or a custom domain. The value is the full Blob service endpoint, including the account where the service expects it in the path (the Azurite emulator embeds the account in the path):

Properties props = new Properties();
props.setProperty("storage.azure.endpoint", "http://127.0.0.1:10000/devstoreaccount1"); // Azurite
props.setProperty("storage.azure.connection-string", "UseDevelopmentStorage=true");

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("az://devstoreaccount1/my-container/"), props)) {
    storage.put("file.bin", new byte[100]);
}

A connection string naming BlobEndpoint or EndpointSuffix sets the endpoint itself, and overrides storage.azure.endpoint.

docs.title: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (HNS)
docs.text:
// abfs:// URI form
try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create(
        "abfss://my-fs@myaccount.dfs.core.windows.net/data/"))) {

    storage.put("a/b/c/file.bin", new byte[100]);

    // Atomic move (HNS only)
    if (storage.capabilities().atomicMove()) {
        storage.move("a/b/c/file.bin", "a/b/d/file.bin");
    }
}

// https:// URL of the dfs endpoint: name the provider
Properties props = new Properties();
props.setProperty("storage.provider", "azure-datalake");
try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create(
        "https://myaccount.dfs.core.windows.net/my-fs/data/"), props)) {
    // ...
}

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
import java.nio.file.Path;

// Flat keyspace bucket
try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("gs://my-bucket/datasets/"))) {
    storage.put("year=2024/file.parquet", Path.of("/local/file.parquet"), WriteOptions.defaults());

    // Hierarchical Namespace bucket: same code path; HNS auto-detected at open.
    System.out.println("Real directories: " + storage.capabilities().realDirectories());
    System.out.println("Atomic move: " + storage.capabilities().atomicMove());
}

Authentication uses Google application default credentials (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS env var, gcloud auth application-default login, GCE/GKE/Cloud Run metadata). Opening fails when none is found. Public buckets need storage.gcs.anonymous=true.

docs.title: Pattern syntax
docs.text:
The single argument to Storage.list(String pattern) is a shell-style glob (or a plain prefix). The longest non-glob prefix seeds the listing; ** (or any / in the glob portion) makes the walk recursive; the pattern filters results client-side with DuckDB-style glob rules: * and ? stay within one path segment, ** crosses /, and **/ also matches zero directories.

// Pure prefix: immediate children of the prefix
storage.list("");                          // root listing
storage.list("data/");                      // immediate children of data/

// Glob characters at the leaf: immediate children with filter
storage.list("data/*.parquet");             // depth-1 .parquet under data/

// ** anywhere: recursive walk
storage.list("data/**");                    // every descendant of data/
storage.list("data/**/*.parquet");          // every .parquet at any depth under data/
storage.list("**.parquet");                 // every .parquet anywhere

// Brace alternation: the '/' in the glob portion implies recursion to reach the matched depth
storage.list("data/{a,b}/file.txt");        // walks data/, matches data/a/file.txt or data/b/file.txt

For pagination and metadata-fetch tuning, use the two-arg overload:

import io.tileverse.storage.ListOptions;

storage.list("data/**", ListOptions.builder().pageSize(500).build());

docs.title: Conditional writes (compare-and-swap)
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.storage.WriteOptions;
import io.tileverse.storage.PreconditionFailedException;

// Create-only (atomic put-if-absent)
try {
    storage.put("locks/leader", new byte[]{1},
            WriteOptions.builder().ifNotExists(true).build());
} catch (PreconditionFailedException e) {
    // Someone else won the race
}

// Compare-and-swap on ETag / generation
String currentEtag = storage.stat("config.json").orElseThrow().etag().orElseThrow();
try {
    storage.put("config.json", newConfigBytes,
            WriteOptions.builder().ifMatchEtag(currentEtag).build());
} catch (PreconditionFailedException e) {
    // Someone else updated the object since we read it
}

docs.title: Tile Matrix Set
docs.text: This module implements the OGC Two Dimensional Tile Matrix Set (17-083r2) standard. It maps coordinates to tiles and back, describes tile pyramids, and reads and writes the JSON and XML encodings of the standard.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
A tile matrix set has one tile matrix per zoom level. A tile matrix is a grid of tiles over the extent of the set, in the units of its CRS. The resolution of a level gives the CRS units per pixel, and the scale denominator follows from it with the standard rendering pixel size of 0.28 mm.

Type Role TileMatrixSet The top-level OGC object: identifier, CRS, extent, and one TileMatrix per zoom level. TileMatrix One zoom level: tile size in pixels, resolution, scale denominator, top-left corner, and matrix dimensions. TilePyramid The grid arithmetic alone, without a CRS: one TileRange per level, with a shared CornerOfOrigin. TileRange A rectangular range of tile indices at one zoom level. Tile One tile: its TileIndex and its extent in CRS units. TileIndex The zoom level z (int), the column x and the row y (long). BoundingBox2D An axis-aligned extent in CRS units. DefaultTileMatrixSets Constants for WebMercatorQuad, WorldCRS84Quad, and older GeoWebCache-style sets. TileMatrixSetIO Reads and writes the JSON (Annex C) and XML (Annex D) encodings.

The module also models the limits and links of the standard: TileMatrixLimits, TileMatrixSetLimits, TileMatrixSetLink, and VariableMatrixWidth.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.tileverse.tilematrixset</groupId>
    <artifactId>tileverse-tilematrixset</artifactId>
</dependency>

The version comes from tileverse-bom, as described in Getting Started.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Find the tiles covering a bounding box:

import io.tileverse.geom.BoundingBox2D;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.DefaultTileMatrixSets;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrix;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSet;

TileMatrixSet tms = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WEB_MERCATOR_QUAD;
TileMatrix matrix = tms.getTileMatrix(12);

// Bounding box in the CRS of the set, here EPSG:3857 meters
BoundingBox2D nyc = BoundingBox2D.extent(-8238000, 4965000, -8230000, 4975000);

matrix.extentToRange(nyc).ifPresent(range -> {
    System.out.println("Tiles needed: " + range.count());
    range.all().forEach(idx ->
        System.out.printf("Fetch z=%d x=%d y=%d%n", idx.z(), idx.x(), idx.y()));
});

docs.title: Component view
docs.text: A TileMatrixSet delegates the grid arithmetic to its TilePyramid, and adds the CRS, the extent, and the resolutions.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Tutorial: pick a standard set, map a coordinate to a tile, iterate over an area, and build a custom set.
  • Tile pyramids and ranges: grid arithmetic without a CRS.
  • Standard tile matrix sets: the bundled sets.
  • OGC compliance and encodings: the mapping to the standard, and the JSON and XML encodings.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: This guide walks through the everyday operations of tileverse-tilematrixset: selecting a tile matrix set, mapping coordinates to tiles, iterating over a region, and building a custom set.

docs.title: 1. Pick a standard set
docs.text:
Standard sets are available as static constants on DefaultTileMatrixSets. Each one has an OGC identifier, a supportedCRS URI, and, where applicable, a wellKnownScaleSet URI.

import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.DefaultTileMatrixSets;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSet;

TileMatrixSet tms = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WEB_MERCATOR_QUAD;

System.out.println(tms.identifier());        // "WebMercatorQuad"
System.out.println(tms.supportedCRS());      // http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/3857
System.out.println(tms.wellKnownScaleSet()); // Optional[http://...GoogleMapsCompatible]

docs.title: 2. Map a coordinate to a tile
docs.text:
coordinateToTile accepts a coordinate in the CRS of the matrix set and returns the tile that contains it. Inputs must already be in the target CRS; use a projection library if you need to convert from longitude/latitude.

import io.tileverse.geom.Coordinate;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.DefaultTileMatrixSets;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSet;
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TileIndex;

TileMatrixSet tms = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WORLD_CRS84_QUAD;

Coordinate london = new Coordinate(-0.1276, 51.5074); // lon/lat in CRS84
TileIndex tile = tms.coordinateToTile(london, 10);

System.out.printf("Tile z=%d x=%d y=%d%n", tile.z(), tile.x(), tile.y());

docs.title: 3. Iterate tiles intersecting an area
docs.text:
TileMatrix.intersection(bbox) returns a matrix restricted to the tiles overlapping the bounding box, and its tiles() stream emits only those tiles. extentToRange(bbox) returns the same tiles as a TileRange of tile indices.

import io.tileverse.geom.BoundingBox2D;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrix;

TileMatrix matrixZ12 = tms.getTileMatrix(12);
BoundingBox2D area = BoundingBox2D.extent(-1.0, 50.0, 1.0, 52.0);

matrixZ12.intersection(area).ifPresent(view ->
    view.tiles().forEach(tile ->
        System.out.println("Processing " + tile.tileIndex())));

docs.title: 4. Build a custom set
docs.text:
The builder requires identifier, CRS, tile pyramid, extent, and resolutions. Optional OGC metadata (title, abstract, keywords, well-known scale set) goes through fluent setters.

import io.tileverse.geom.BoundingBox2D;
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.CornerOfOrigin;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSet;
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TilePyramid;
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TileRange;

double[] resolutions = {0.703125, 0.3515625, 0.17578125};
TilePyramid pyramid = TilePyramid.builder()
        .cornerOfOrigin(CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT)
        .level(TileRange.of(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT))
        .level(TileRange.of(0, 0, 3, 1, 1, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT))
        .level(TileRange.of(0, 0, 7, 3, 2, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT))
        .build();

TileMatrixSet custom = TileMatrixSet.builder()
        .identifier("MyCustomSet")
        .title("Custom 4326 set, zooms 0-2")
        .crs("EPSG:4326")
        .tilePyramid(pyramid)
        .tileSize(256, 256)
        .extent(BoundingBox2D.extent(-180, -90, 180, 90))
        .resolutions(resolutions)
        .build();

docs.title: Standard Tile Matrix Sets
docs.text: DefaultTileMatrixSets exposes the most common tile matrix sets as immutable static constants. Each instance is fully populated with an OGC identifier, the supportedCRS URI, and, when applicable, the matching well-known scale set URI.

docs.title: WebMercatorQuad
docs.text:
The OGC standard set used by Google Maps, OpenStreetMap, Mapbox, Leaflet, OpenLayers and almost every web mapping client.

  • identifier: WebMercatorQuad
  • CRS: EPSG:3857 (Spherical Mercator, meters)
  • wellKnownScaleSet: http://www.opengis.net/def/wkss/OGC/1.0/GoogleMapsCompatible
  • Origin: top-left
  • Structure: 1 tile at zoom 0, four child tiles at each subsequent level
TileMatrixSet tms = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WEB_MERCATOR_QUAD;
TileMatrixSet tms512 = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WEB_MERCATOR_QUADx2; // 512 px tiles

docs.title: WorldCRS84Quad
docs.text:
OGC standard set for geographic (longitude/latitude) tile pyramids. Useful when you want to avoid reprojection to Web Mercator.

  • identifier: WorldCRS84Quad
  • CRS: CRS:84 (WGS84 lon/lat)
  • wellKnownScaleSet: http://www.opengis.net/def/wkss/OGC/1.0/GoogleCRS84Quad
  • Origin: top-left
  • Structure: 2x1 tiles at zoom 0 covering [-180, -90, 180, 90]
TileMatrixSet tms = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WORLD_CRS84_QUAD;
TileMatrixSet tms512 = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WORLD_CRS84_QUADx2; // 512 px tiles

docs.title: Legacy GeoWebCache-style sets
docs.text:
These match the GeoWebCache resolution arrays used by older deployments. They share the underlying CRS with the OGC sets above. WORLD_EPSG3857 and WORLD_EPSG3857x2 declare the GoogleMapsCompatible well-known scale set, and the EPSG:4326 sets declare none.

Constant Identifier CRS Tile size WORLD_EPSG3857 WORLD_EPSG3857 EPSG:3857 256 WORLD_EPSG3857x2 WORLD_EPSG3857x2 EPSG:3857 512 WORLD_EPSG4326 WORLD_EPSG4326 EPSG:4326 256 WORLD_EPSG4326x2 WORLD_EPSG4326x2 EPSG:4326 512

docs.title: Common properties
docs.text:
Every standard set is thread-safe and immutable, and exposes:

  • the canonical identifier() (mandatory in OGC TMS 2D),
  • a supportedCRS() URI suitable for OGC API - Tiles consumption,
  • resolution(int z) values, with the matching scale denominator given by getTileMatrix(z).scaleDenominator() and calculated from the standard 0.28 mm rendering pixel size,
  • a boundingBox() covering the full CRS extent,
  • a tilePyramid() exposing the per-level tile ranges.

docs.title: Tile Pyramids and Ranges
docs.text: TileMatrixSet is the top-level OGC TMS object, but its grid structure is stored as a separate TilePyramid. The pyramid can also be used on its own when you need grid arithmetic without spatial coordinates.

docs.title: TilePyramid
docs.text:
A pyramid is a collection of TileRange levels sharing a single CornerOfOrigin. Construct one through TilePyramid.builder() or with the TilePyramid.of(...) factories.

import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.CornerOfOrigin;
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TilePyramid;
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TileRange;

TilePyramid pyramid = TilePyramid.builder()
        .cornerOfOrigin(CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT)
        .level(TileRange.of(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT)) // z=0
        .level(TileRange.of(0, 0, 1, 1, 1, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT)) // z=1
        .level(TileRange.of(0, 0, 3, 3, 2, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT)) // z=2
        .build();

int min = pyramid.minZoomLevel();
int max = pyramid.maxZoomLevel();
TileRange level1 = pyramid.tileRange(1);

TilePyramid trimmed = pyramid.subset(1, 2); // keeps levels 1 and 2 only

docs.title: TileRange
docs.text:
TileRange describes a rectangular region of tiles at a single zoom level. It stores only the corner indices and is cheap to create, even for large pyramids.

TileRange range = TileRange.of(0, 0, 1, 1, 10, CornerOfOrigin.TOP_LEFT);

range.count();                // 4
range.spanX();                // 2
range.spanY();                // 2
range.all().forEach(System.out::println); // streams the 4 TileIndex values

Ranges support set-style operations: intersection, union, contains, and traversal helpers first(), last(), next(index), prev(index). They are the building blocks of every spatial query exposed by TileMatrix.

docs.title: Sparse ranges
docs.text: When TileRange.union or TileMatrix.union combines ranges into a shape that is not rectangular, the result is a sparse range. Code uses it through the same TileRange and TileMatrix methods as a rectangular range.

docs.title: CornerOfOrigin
docs.text:
Tile pyramids can index tiles from either the top-left (the OGC default and the convention used by most web maps and PMTiles) or the bottom-left (the older TMS/WMS-C convention). TilePyramid.builder(), TilePyramid.of(...) and TileRange.of(...) use BOTTOM_LEFT unless a corner is given.

import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.CornerOfOrigin;

CornerOfOrigin origin = pyramid.cornerOfOrigin();

TileMatrix honours the origin of the pyramid when it converts between CRS coordinates and tile indices. Callers do not flip the Y axis themselves.

docs.title: OGC Compliance
docs.text: tileverse-tilematrixset implements the data model and the JSON/XML encodings defined by OGC Two Dimensional Tile Matrix Set 17-083r2. The summary excerpt of the spec is kept alongside the source as tileverse-tilematrixset/spec.md.

docs.title: Data model mapping

docs.title: Scale algebra
docs.text:
CrsUnits provides the standard 0.28 mm rendering pixel conversions defined by OGC 17-083r2 clause 8 (Annex B):

double scaleDenominator = CrsUnits.resolutionToScaleDenominator(resolution, "EPSG:3857");
double resolution       = CrsUnits.scaleDenominatorToResolution(scaleDenominator, "EPSG:4326");

It recognises the CRSs of the bundled standard sets (EPSG:3857, EPSG:4326, CRS:84) and defaults to a meters-per-unit coefficient of 1 for unknown CRSs.

docs.title: JSON encoding (Annex C)
docs.text:
TileMatrixSetIO round-trips through the Jackson records in io.tileverse.jackson.databind.tms.v1, using the field names from the JSON Schema:

import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.DefaultTileMatrixSets;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSet;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSetIO;

TileMatrixSet tms = DefaultTileMatrixSets.WEB_MERCATOR_QUAD;
String json = TileMatrixSetIO.toJSON(tms);

// Or stream-based:
TileMatrixSetIO.writeJSON(tms, System.out);
TileMatrixSet parsed = TileMatrixSetIO.readJSON(json);

The serialised output follows the OGC structure:

{
  "id": "WebMercatorQuad",
  "crs": "http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/3857",
  "wellKnownScaleSet": "http://www.opengis.net/def/wkss/OGC/1.0/GoogleMapsCompatible",
  "boundingBox": {
    "lowerLeft": [-20037508.3427892, -20037508.3427892],
    "upperRight": [20037508.3427892, 20037508.3427892],
    "crs": "http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/3857"
  },
  "tileMatrices": [
    {
      "id": "0",
      "scaleDenominator": 559082264.0287178,
      "cellSize": 156543.0339280410,
      "pointOfOrigin": [-20037508.3427892, 20037508.3427892],
      "tileWidth": 256,
      "tileHeight": 256,
      "matrixWidth": 1,
      "matrixHeight": 1
    }
  ]
}

The reader accepts JSON that declares either cellSize, scaleDenominator, or both, and normalizes a URI-form CRS such as http://www.opengis.net/def/crs/EPSG/0/3857 back to EPSG:3857 while preserving the original URI in supportedCRS().

docs.title: XML encoding (Annex D)
docs.text:
XML support uses StAX, requiring no extra dependencies:

import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSet;
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.TileMatrixSetIO;

TileMatrixSet tms = TileMatrixSetIO.readXML(inputStream);
TileMatrixSetIO.writeXML(tms, outputStream);

The writer emits a single default namespace (http://www.opengis.net/tms/1.0). The reader is namespace-agnostic and also accepts the historical WMTS 1.0 / OWS 1.1 element layout.

docs.title: Vector Tiles
docs.text: This module encodes and decodes Mapbox Vector Tiles (MVT), version 2.1. It converts between the protobuf encoding and a VectorTile model with JTS geometries.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
A vector tile holds named layers, and a layer holds features. A feature has an optional id, attributes, and a geometry. Geometries are in tile coordinates: the origin is the top-left corner of the tile, y grows downward, and the extent of the layer, usually 4096, spans the tile.

Decoding is lazy. A feature decodes its geometry and its attributes on first access.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.tileverse.vectortiles</groupId>
    <artifactId>tileverse-vectortiles</artifactId>
</dependency>

The version comes from tileverse-bom, as described in Getting Started.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Decode MVT bytes, for example a tile read from a PMTiles archive:

import io.tileverse.vectortile.model.VectorTile;
import io.tileverse.vectortile.mvt.VectorTileCodec;
import java.util.Map;
import org.locationtech.jts.geom.Geometry;

VectorTileCodec codec = new VectorTileCodec();
VectorTile tile = codec.decode(mvtBytes);

for (VectorTile.Layer layer : tile.getLayers()) {
    System.out.println("Layer: " + layer.getName());
    layer.getFeatures().forEach(feature -> {
        Geometry geometry = feature.getGeometry();
        Map<String, Object> attributes = feature.getAttributes();
    });
}

Build a tile from JTS geometries and encode it:

import io.tileverse.vectortile.mvt.VectorTileBuilder;

VectorTileBuilder builder = new VectorTileBuilder();
builder.layer()
        .name("buildings")
        .feature()
            .id(123)
            .geometry(polygon)       // in tile coordinates
            .attribute("height", 50)
            .build()                 // returns the LayerBuilder
        .build();                    // adds the layer, returns the VectorTileBuilder

byte[] encoded = codec.encode(builder.build());

docs.title: Component view
docs.text: VectorTileCodec encodes and decodes between MVT bytes and the VectorTile model. VectorTileBuilder builds VectorTile instances from JTS geometries.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Encode vector tiles: build tiles, configure clipping and simplification, and write the bytes.
  • Decode vector tiles: read layers and features, and filter features without decoding their geometries.

docs.title: Decoding Vector Tiles
docs.text: VectorTileCodec decodes raw Mapbox Vector Tile bytes into a VectorTile model with JTS Geometry instances attached to each feature. The codec is stateless and thread-safe; instantiate once and reuse.

docs.title: Pick an input shape
docs.text:
VectorTileCodec accepts three inputs:

VectorTileCodec codec = new VectorTileCodec();

VectorTile fromBytes  = codec.decode(byte[] data);
VectorTile fromBuffer = codec.decode(ByteBuffer data);  // reads from data.position() to data.limit()
VectorTile fromStream = codec.decode(InputStream in);   // reads to the end; the caller closes the stream

Prefer decode(InputStream) when the source is already a stream (HTTP body, channel-backed input). It avoids materializing the encoded bytes in a transient array.

docs.title: Walk layers and features
docs.text:
VectorTile tile = codec.decode(rawBytes);

for (VectorTile.Layer layer : tile.getLayers()) {
    System.out.println("Layer: " + layer.getName());
    System.out.println("Extent: " + layer.getExtent());  // tile coordinate extent, usually 4096

    layer.getFeatures().forEach(feature -> {
        long id = feature.getId();
        Geometry geom = feature.getGeometry();          // JTS Geometry in tile coordinates
        Map<String, Object> props = feature.getAttributes();
    });
}

VectorTile.Layer.Feature.getGeometry() returns a JTS Geometry whose coordinates are in the layer's own tile extent (getExtent(), typically 4096). Origin is the top-left of the tile, y grows downward. To project into a real-world CRS you need the tile's (z, x, y) and the matching TileMatrixSet (see Tile Matrix Set).

docs.title: Filter features without materializing geometries
docs.text:
Geometry decoding is the expensive step in MVT parsing. A feature decodes its geometry on the first call to getGeometry(). A predicate reading only attributes leaves the geometries of rejected features undecoded:

import java.util.function.Predicate;

Predicate<VectorTile.Layer.Feature> roadsOnly =
        f -> "primary".equals(f.getAttributes().get("type"));

tile.getFeatures("roads", roadsOnly, VectorTileCodec.newGeometryReader())
        .forEach(f -> process(f.getGeometry()));

The Layer.getFeatures(Predicate) and Layer.getFeatures(Predicate, GeometryReader) overloads do the same on a layer you already hold.

docs.title: Cross-layer queries
docs.text:
Convenience methods on VectorTile route to the right layer:

tile.getFeatures("roads").forEach(...);                  // all features of one layer
tile.getFeatures().forEach(...);                          // every feature of every layer
tile.getLayer("buildings").ifPresent(layer -> ...);       // null-safe layer lookup

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
decode(...) throws IOException when the bytes are not a valid MVT protobuf message. Geometry commands are decoded later, on the first call to getGeometry(). A corrupt command stream makes that call throw an IllegalArgumentException or IllegalStateException.

try {
    VectorTile tile = codec.decode(bytes);
} catch (IOException e) {
    log.warn("Skipping malformed tile {}/{}/{}: {}", z, x, y, e.getMessage());
}

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Encoding Vector Tiles for the reverse direction.
  • Tile Stores Reference for PMTilesVectorTileStore, which decodes tiles served from a PMTiles archive and gives you VectorTile directly.

docs.title: Encoding Vector Tiles
docs.text: VectorTileBuilder assembles a VectorTile from JTS Geometry instances; VectorTileCodec.encode(...) serializes the result to MVT bytes.

docs.title: Build a tile
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.vectortile.model.VectorTile;
import io.tileverse.vectortile.mvt.VectorTileBuilder;
import io.tileverse.vectortile.mvt.VectorTileCodec;
import org.locationtech.jts.geom.Geometry;

VectorTileBuilder builder = new VectorTileBuilder();

builder.layer()
        .name("buildings")
        .feature()
            .id(123)
            .geometry(buildingPolygon)
            .attribute("height", 50)
            .attribute("type", "residential")
            .build()       // returns LayerBuilder
        .build();          // returns VectorTileBuilder

VectorTile tile = builder.build();

LayerBuilder.feature() opens a FeatureBuilder; chain .id(...) / .geometry(...) / .attribute(...) / .attributes(Map) then call .build() to attach the feature to its layer and return the LayerBuilder for the next feature.

docs.title: Shorthand for many features
docs.text:
When you have a stream of (properties, geometry) pairs (e.g. rows read from another source), the LayerBuilder.feature(Map, Geometry [, long id]) overloads skip the inner builder:

rows.forEach(row -> roadsLayer.feature(row.attributes(), row.geometry()));

docs.title: Encode to bytes
docs.text:
Three target shapes:

VectorTileCodec codec = new VectorTileCodec();

byte[] bytes = codec.encode(tile);                       // heap byte[]
codec.encode(tile, OutputStream sink);                   // streaming
codec.encode(tile, ByteBuffer sink);                     // pre-sized buffer

The OutputStream overload is the right choice when you're piping straight to an HTTP response: no intermediate heap copy.

encode accepts the tiles built by VectorTileBuilder and the tiles returned by decode. Another VectorTile implementation fails with UnsupportedOperationException.

docs.title: Configure encoding
docs.text:
VectorTileBuilder has tile-wide settings. Set them before adding features: each feature is clipped, simplified and encoded when its FeatureBuilder.build() runs, with the settings in effect at that moment.

builder
    .setExtent(4096)                          // tile coordinate extent (default 4096)
    .setClipBuffer(64)                        // tile units of buffer around the tile bbox (default 32)
    .setAutoIncrementIds(true)                // assign ids automatically when features omit them
    .setSimplificationDistanceTolerance(1.0); // Douglas-Peucker tolerance in tile units

These are tile-wide, not per-layer. Tune them once for the output dataset.

docs.title: Coordinates and units
docs.text: The geometries you pass to the builder must already be in tile coordinates: origin at the tile's top-left, y growing downward, extent given by setExtent(...) (typically 4096). If your source is in a CRS (EPSG:3857, etc.), project to tile coordinates first using the matching TileMatrixSet. See Tile Matrix Set.

docs.text:

  • MVT v2.1 spec for the binary format.

docs.title: Versatiles
docs.text:
This module reads VersaTiles containers, a single-file archive format for map tiles. It implements version 2 of the container specification.

The module reads archives and does not write them. To create an archive, use the versatiles command-line tool. For example, versatiles convert input.pmtiles output.versatiles converts a PMTiles archive.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Cloud-optimized reads: a tile costs one range request once the index of its block is cached.
  • Storage agnostic: works with the RangeReader backends of tileverse-storage: local file, HTTP, S3, Azure Blob, and GCS.
  • Vector and raster tiles: VersatilesReader returns the decompressed bytes of tiles, whatever their format. VersatilesVectorTileStore decodes Mapbox Vector Tiles to VectorTile objects, and VersatilesRasterTileStore decodes PNG, JPEG, and WebP tiles to RenderedImage objects.
  • Compression: reads uncompressed, gzip, Brotli, and Zstandard archives.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
A Versatiles container has four parts:

  1. Header: 66 bytes at the start of the file. It records the tile format, the compression, the zoom range, the bounding box, and the location of the other parts.
  2. Metadata: a TileJSON document, compressed like the tiles.
  3. Blocks: the tiles of one zoom level are grouped in blocks of up to 256 x 256 tiles. A block stores its tile bodies, followed by a tile index with the positions of the tiles inside the block.
  4. Block index: one 33-byte entry per block, at the end of the file.

To read a tile, the reader finds its block in the block index, loads the tile index of that block, and reads the tile body. The block index is read once, when the reader opens the archive. Tile indexes stay in a cache, and the body of a tile takes a single range request.

Tiles are addressed with the XYZ scheme: zoom level, column from west to east, and row from north to south. Row 0 is the northernmost row, as in PMTiles and in web map clients.

The block index and the tile indexes are always compressed with Brotli. The metadata and the tile bodies use the compression declared in the header: none, gzip, Brotli, or Zstandard. The reader decompresses tiles before it returns them.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.tileverse.versatiles</groupId>
    <artifactId>tileverse-versatiles</artifactId>
</dependency>

The version comes from tileverse-bom, as described in Getting Started. Local files and HTTP work out of the box. S3, Azure and GCS URIs need tileverse-storage-all, or the matching tileverse-storage-s3, tileverse-storage-azure or tileverse-storage-gcs module, next to tileverse-versatiles.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TileIndex;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.VersatilesHeader;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.VersatilesReader;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.Optional;

try (VersatilesReader reader = VersatilesReader.open(Path.of("data/map.versatiles"))) {
    VersatilesHeader header = reader.getHeader();
    System.out.println("Tile format: " + header.tileFormat());
    System.out.println("Zoom levels: " + header.minZoom() + " to " + header.maxZoom());

    // The buffer is ready to read, do not flip it
    Optional<ByteBuffer> tile = reader.getTile(TileIndex.zxy(0, 0, 0));
}

VersatilesReader.open(URI) accepts the URIs supported by tileverse-storage, such as s3://bucket/map.versatiles or https://example.com/map.versatiles.

docs.title: Component view
docs.text: VersatilesReader is the low-level type. It reads the header, finds the block of a tile in the BlockIndex, finds the tile inside its block through the TileIndexCache, and returns the decompressed tile bytes. It can also stream them through an IOFunction supplied by the caller. VersatilesVectorTileStore and VersatilesRasterTileStore wrap a VersatilesReader and decode tiles to VectorTile and RenderedImage objects.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Read Versatiles archives: open archives in cloud storage, read tiles, and decode them with the tile stores.
  • Format support: tile formats, compression, exceptions, and caches.

docs.title: Reading Versatiles archives
docs.text: This guide shows how to open a Versatiles archive, read its tiles, and decode them.

docs.title: Open an archive
docs.text:
VersatilesReader.open opens the Storage of the parent location and gets a RangeReader for the file. Closing the VersatilesReader closes both. The call accepts a local path, or a URI with a scheme supported by tileverse-storage. The cloud schemes need their storage module, as described in Installation.

import io.tileverse.versatiles.VersatilesReader;
import java.net.URI;
import java.nio.file.Path;

// Local file
VersatilesReader fileReader = VersatilesReader.open(Path.of("map.versatiles"));

// HTTP
VersatilesReader httpReader = VersatilesReader.open(URI.create("https://example.com/map.versatiles"));

// S3, Azure, and GCS use the same call
VersatilesReader s3Reader = VersatilesReader.open(URI.create("s3://bucket/map.versatiles"));

To configure the storage backend, for example its region, credentials, or endpoint, pass a StorageConfig. The storage configuration guide lists the parameters.

import io.tileverse.storage.StorageConfig;

StorageConfig config = new StorageConfig(URI.create("s3://bucket/map.versatiles"))
        .setParameter("storage.s3.region", "eu-central-1");

try (VersatilesReader reader = VersatilesReader.open(config)) {
    // ...
}

To read through a RangeReader opened by your own code, pass it to the constructor. The VersatilesReader takes ownership of the RangeReader and closes it in close(). The following example caches the ranges read from S3 in memory:

import io.tileverse.storage.RangeReader;
import io.tileverse.storage.Storage;
import io.tileverse.storage.StorageFactory;
import io.tileverse.storage.cache.CachingRangeReader;

try (Storage storage = StorageFactory.open(URI.create("s3://bucket/"));
        VersatilesReader reader = new VersatilesReader(CachingRangeReader.of(storage.openRangeReader("map.versatiles")))) {
    // ...
}

Opening an archive reads its header, its metadata, and its block index. An InvalidHeaderException means the file is not a Versatiles 2 container.

docs.title: Read the header and metadata
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.geom.BoundingBox2D;
import io.tileverse.jackson.databind.tilejson.v3.VectorLayer;
import io.tileverse.jackson.databind.versatiles.v2.VersatilesMetadata;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.Compression;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.TileFormat;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.VersatilesHeader;

VersatilesHeader header = reader.getHeader();
TileFormat format = header.tileFormat();         // PBF, PNG, JPEG, WEBP, ...
String mimeType = format.mimeType();             // "application/x-protobuf", "image/webp", ...
Compression compression = header.compression();  // NONE, GZIP, BROTLI, or ZSTD
int minZoom = header.minZoom();
int maxZoom = header.maxZoom();
BoundingBox2D bounds = header.geographicBoundingBox();  // WGS84 longitude and latitude, in degrees

VersatilesMetadata metadata = reader.getMetadata();
String name = metadata.name();
List<VectorLayer> layers = metadata.vectorLayers();

String json = reader.getMetadataAsString();  // the TileJSON document as stored in the archive

VersatilesMetadata exposes the common TileJSON fields. The fields without a dedicated getter are in metadata.extras().

docs.title: Read tiles
docs.text:
getTile returns the bytes of a tile after decompression, or an empty Optional when the archive has no tile at that position. The buffer is ready to read. Do not flip it.

import io.tileverse.tiling.pyramid.TileIndex;
import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
import java.util.Optional;

Optional<ByteBuffer> tile = reader.getTile(TileIndex.zxy(14, 8261, 6050));

A position outside the zoom range of the archive, or outside the tile grid of its zoom level, returns an empty Optional.

To decode a tile as it is read, pass a function to getTile. The function receives the decompressed bytes as an InputStream, and getTile returns its result. This overload avoids a copy of the tile into a ByteBuffer:

import io.tileverse.io.IOFunction;
import java.io.InputStream;

IOFunction<InputStream, byte[]> toBytes = InputStream::readAllBytes;
Optional<byte[]> bytes = reader.getTile(TileIndex.zxy(14, 8261, 6050), toBytes);

VersatilesReader is thread-safe. Several threads can read tiles from one reader at the same time.

docs.title: Decode tiles with a tile store
docs.text:
The tile stores wrap a VersatilesReader and implement the TileStore<T> API described in the Tile Stores Reference. They decode tiles to the payload type of the store:

Tile format Store Payload PBF (Mapbox Vector Tiles) VersatilesVectorTileStore io.tileverse.vectortile.model.VectorTile PNG, JPEG, WEBP, AVIF VersatilesRasterTileStore java.awt.image.RenderedImage

A store checks the tile format of the archive when it is created. It throws UnsupportedTileFormatException when the archive holds another format. To pick the store from the archive:

import io.tileverse.tiling.store.TileStore;

TileStore<?> store = reader.getTileFormat() == TileFormat.PBF
        ? new VersatilesVectorTileStore(reader)
        : new VersatilesRasterTileStore(reader);

The stores borrow the reader. Close the reader when you are done; a store holds no other resources.

The tile matrix set of a store ends at zoom level 24, the last level of WebMercatorQuad. The reader returns the tiles of deeper levels, outside the stores.

docs.title: Read vector tiles
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.tiling.matrix.Tile;
import io.tileverse.tiling.store.TileData;
import io.tileverse.vectortile.model.VectorTile;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.store.VersatilesVectorTileStore;

try (VersatilesReader reader = VersatilesReader.open(uri)) {
    VersatilesVectorTileStore store = new VersatilesVectorTileStore(reader);

    Tile tile = store.matrixSet().getTileMatrix(14).tile(TileIndex.xyz(8261, 6050, 14)).orElseThrow();
    Optional<TileData<VectorTile>> data = store.loadTile(tile);

    data.ifPresent(td -> {
        VectorTile vectorTile = td.data();
        // walk layers and features...
    });
}

store.getVectorLayersMetadata() returns the vector_layers of the archive metadata.

docs.title: Read raster tiles
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.versatiles.store.VersatilesRasterTileStore;
import java.awt.image.RenderedImage;

try (VersatilesReader reader = VersatilesReader.open(uri)) {
    VersatilesRasterTileStore store = new VersatilesRasterTileStore(reader);

    System.out.println("MIME type: " + store.mimeType());  // "image/webp", "image/png", ...

    Tile tile = store.matrixSet().getTileMatrix(10).tile(TileIndex.xyz(885, 412, 10)).orElseThrow();
    Optional<TileData<RenderedImage>> data = store.loadTile(tile);
}

PNG and JPEG decoders come with the JDK, and tileverse-versatiles brings a WebP decoder for javax.imageio. AVIF has no bundled decoder. Without an ImageIO plugin for AVIF, the raster store refuses AVIF archives with UnsupportedTileFormatException.

loadTile reports I/O errors as UncheckedIOException, because the TileStore API declares no checked exceptions.

docs.title: Share caches across readers
docs.text:
A reader keeps the tile indexes of recently read blocks in a cache. The vector store also caches decoded tiles. Both caches belong to CacheManager.getDefault() unless you set another CacheManager:

import io.tileverse.cache.CacheManager;

CacheManager cacheManager = CacheManager.newInstance();
reader.cacheManager(cacheManager);

// For a store, this sets the cache manager of the store and of its reader
VersatilesVectorTileStore store = new VersatilesVectorTileStore(reader).cacheManager(cacheManager);

Readers of the same archive share entries in the same CacheManager. The Format support reference lists the cache names and bounds.

docs.title: Handle errors
docs.text:
import io.tileverse.storage.StorageException;
import io.tileverse.versatiles.InvalidHeaderException;
import java.io.IOException;

try (VersatilesReader reader = VersatilesReader.open(uri)) {
    Optional<ByteBuffer> tile = reader.getTile(TileIndex.zxy(zoom, x, y));
} catch (InvalidHeaderException e) {
    // Not a Versatiles 2 container, or a header with an unknown tile format or compression
} catch (StorageException e) {
    // The storage failed; NotFoundException when the file is missing
} catch (IOException e) {
    // A damaged index, or a file ending before a part it declares
}

StorageException (in io.tileverse.storage) is unchecked.

docs.title: Performance tips
docs.text:
1. Reuse readers. Opening a reader reads the header, the metadata, and the block index.
  2. Cache remote reads. Wrap the RangeReader of a remote archive in a CachingRangeReader, as shown in Open an archive.
  3. Read neighboring tiles together. The first tile read from a block loads the tile index of the block. The following tiles of that block reuse it from the cache.

docs.title: Format support
docs.text: This page lists the parts of the Versatiles container specification supported by tileverse-versatiles, with the classes, exceptions, and caches involved.

docs.title: Container version
docs.text: The reader supports version 2 of the container format. A version 2 file starts with the ASCII magic versatiles_v02. Other files fail to open with InvalidHeaderException.

docs.title: Tile formats
docs.text:
The header records the format of the tile bodies. VersatilesReader.getTile returns the tile bodies, whatever their format. The tile stores decode the formats listed in the last column.

Code TileFormat MIME type isVector() Decoded by 0x00 BIN application/octet-stream no - 0x10 PNG image/png no VersatilesRasterTileStore 0x11 JPEG image/jpeg no VersatilesRasterTileStore 0x12 WEBP image/webp no VersatilesRasterTileStore 0x13 AVIF image/avif no VersatilesRasterTileStore, with an AVIF plugin for ImageIO 0x14 SVG image/svg+xml no - 0x20 PBF application/x-protobuf yes VersatilesVectorTileStore 0x21 GEOJSON application/geo+json yes - 0x22 TOPOJSON application/topo+json yes - 0x23 JSON application/json no -

PNG and JPEG decoders come with the JDK. The WebP decoder comes from the com.github.usefulness:webp-imageio dependency of the module. The raster store refuses an archive when no ImageIO decoder reads its format.

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
Code Compression Applies to 0x00 NONE metadata and tile bodies 0x01 GZIP metadata and tile bodies 0x02 BROTLI metadata and tile bodies 0x03 ZSTD metadata and tile bodies

The header declares the compression of the metadata and of the tile bodies. The block index and the tile indexes are always compressed with Brotli, regardless of the header. The reader decompresses tiles before it returns them.

docs.title: Tile coordinates
docs.text:
Tiles use the XYZ scheme of web maps, in the WebMercatorQuad tile matrix set: row 0 is the northernmost row. getTile returns an empty Optional for a zoom level outside the range of the archive, for a negative column or row, and for a position without a tile.

The tile matrix set of a store ends at zoom level 24, the last level of WebMercatorQuad. getTile reads deeper levels too.

The header does not record the tile size. The raster store reads the size of the first tile when it is created, and an archive of 512 px tiles gets the WebMercatorQuadx2 tile matrix set.

docs.title: Archives written by the versatiles tool
docs.text:
The versatiles tool writes two kinds of files outside the specification. The reader accepts both:

  • An inverted bounding box, with a minimum above its maximum, when a conversion uses a bounding box outside the data. VersatilesHeader.geographicBoundingBox() then returns the bounds of the world.
  • A block index of length zero for an archive without tiles. Such an archive opens, and getTile returns an empty Optional.

docs.title: Reads
docs.text:
Operation Range requests Open an archive 3: the header, the metadata, and the block index Read a tile, tile index cached 1 Read a tile, tile index not cached 2: the tile index of the block, then the tile

An archive without metadata, or without tiles, takes one request less to open. The reader reads a part of the archive in one request and decompresses it in memory.

docs.title: Caches
docs.text:
Cache Contents Bounds tileverse-versatiles-tile-index-cache Tile indexes of recently read blocks, one sub-cache per archive 5% of the maximum heap; an entry expires 30 seconds after its last use tileverse-vectortile-cache Decoded tiles of VersatilesVectorTileStore, shared with the other vector tile stores 15% of the maximum heap; an entry expires 10 seconds after its last use

Both caches belong to CacheManager.getDefault(), unless cacheManager(CacheManager) sets another manager on the reader or on the store. The block index is not cached: the reader reads it once and keeps it until it is closed.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
Exception Thrown when InvalidHeaderException The file is not a version 2 container, is shorter than the header, or has a header field outside the specification: an unknown tile format or compression code, a reversed zoom range, or a section longer than 2 GiB. UnsupportedTileFormatException A tile store cannot decode the tile format of the archive, or no ImageIO decoder reads it. IllegalArgumentException A tile store is created over an archive with only zoom levels deeper than 24. IOException The file ends before a part it declares, or the block index or a tile index is damaged. StorageException The storage fails. Its subclass NotFoundException means the file is missing.

InvalidHeaderException and UnsupportedTileFormatException extend IOException. StorageException is unchecked. The loadTile method of the tile stores wraps I/O errors in UncheckedIOException.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• The reader loads the metadata into one buffer, and the block index into another. A Java array limits a buffer to 2 GiB.
  • The module does not write archives. The versatiles tool converts other tile containers, such as PMTiles and MBTiles, to Versatiles containers.
